newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat condition rating declines further.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat condition rating declines further.

text.p: The condition of Texas wheat declined further in the week ended Sunday as stem and head freeze damage to wheat plants became more evident, the state agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop weather report.
Statewide, wheat was rated 24 percent good to excellent, down from 32 percent good to excellent a week ago. The rest of the crop was rated 39 fair and 37 poor to very poor.
Texas remained dry during most of the week. A strong cold front moved through late in the week, bringing moderate to heavy rainfall to many areas and once again stalling fieldwork.

"Damage to late boot (wheat) fields may not be as severe as earlier indicated," the report said. "The recent rains... should benefit the crop. However, open, sunny conditions are very much needed as the crop begins to dry down."

Corn planting continued until late in the week. Statewide, corn was 61 percent planted versus 72 a year ago and 71 on a 5-year average. Corn condition was rated 51 percent good to excellent, down from 60 percent a week ago.
Sorghum planting advanced to 49 percent complete versus 53 a year ago and 43 last week. Condition was rated 60 percent good to excellent versus 54 last week.
Cotton planting was active in central Texas, and statewide cotton planting advanced to 16 percent complete versus 12 percent a week ago and 17 a year ago.
